text:
Anya: quick follow-up from the RFC sync — we need a clear service boundary for dashboard queries. I propose: Query service = authoritative RBAC + row-level enforcement + aggregation primitives. Console = UI projection, client-side small filters, and opt-in fast paths (precomputed aggregates). thoughts?

Mike: agree that Query service should be the source of truth for row-level access. Clients enforcing RBAC leads to audit gaps. Query should never return rows outside role constraints.

Taylor: perf question: per-user RBAC + heavy aggregation could blow up p95 for large tenants. do we have a caching or precompute strategy that still preserves correctness?

Sanja: suggestion: two-path model. Default live path: Query enforces RBAC and runs live aggregates. Fast path: role-aware precomputation (sharded aggregates or MVs) that dashboards opt into. Precompute only for high-traffic dashboards.

Oliver: to control MV explosion, use a bounded set of role buckets (e.g., admin/writer/reader + team buckets up to N), and namespace as: sharded_agg:{org}:{dashboard_hash}:{role_bucket}. Use TTL + LRU eviction driven by hit counters.

Anya: important correctness callout: never apply aggregate before RBAC unless the aggregate granularity permits safe recomposition. filter -> aggregate must hold in all paths that touch live data.

Taylor: if serving cached aggregates, store them partitioned by tenant and role_bucket so we can combine only the partitions the caller is allowed to see. otherwise counts leak.

Sanja: implementation sketch for Query API (shared rewrite lib so private deployments can vendor):
```
POST /v1/console/query
{
  "query_id": "dash_usage_v2",
  "params": {"range": "30d", "granularity": "day"},
  "org_id": "o-987",
  "role_sig": "hmac:sha256:abcdef..."
}
// server validates role_sig against org secret -> rewrites query to include row_predicate(org_id, role_bucket) -> execute
```
Make the rewrite code a small well-tested library (js/py/go) so private stacks can include it.

Mike: security: role_sig must be HMAC with an org-scoped key (rotatable). never accept raw role names from the client. also sign the query_id to prevent replay.

Oliver: add HTTP header `X-Console-Role-Signature` for the HMAC and `X-Console-Debug-Role` for dev-only responses. ensure debug header stripped from production logs.

Anya: telemetry proposals: emit counters/histograms in Query: queries_validated, queries_rewritten, queries_denied_rbac, queries_served_from_precompute, precompute_rebuilds, precompute_evictions, query_latency_p50_p95. Tag by dashboard and org.

Taylor: UX contract: we need to differentiate access denial vs partial/stale results. Use 403 for deny; 206 (Partial Content) + `X-Console-Partial-Reason: stale-precompute` for partial fast-path. Console should show a clear banner when data may be stale.

Sanja: include in query response a `cache_info` blob for the Console UI: e.g. `{"source":"precompute","freshness_ms":"60000"}` so the frontend can display freshness and a refresh button. (Strip sensitive bits in logs.)

Mike: rollout: start correctness-first (live queries) with conservative perf SLOs, then opt-in dashboards to precompute.Suggested latency targets: live path p50 < 120ms, p95 < 800ms; precompute path p50 < 40ms, p95 < 200ms. include dashboard-level SLOs.

Oliver: operationally, precompute refresh jobs must back off if the tenant is under load. also expose an admin API to prime or rebuild a specific precompute shard for debugging.

Anya: one more thing: signing and role encoding. Use HMAC(role_string || org_id || nonce) with replay window. role_bucket should be canonicalized (e.g., role:admin, team:123). Store role-to-bucket mapping in the policy store.

Taylor: dev experience: Console team needs clear error surfaces for 206 vs 403; also a tooltip explaining staleness. Add a debug mode to surface which partitions were used for a response (dev only).

Sanja: cost tradeoffs: precompute reduces query CPU but increases storage and rebuild IO. we'll gate precompute creation on a cost/benefit rule: hit_rate > X and average query latency > Y -> create precompute.

Mike: perf measurement: add synthetic dashboards and per-tenant canaries to validate p95 under load before enabling precompute in prod.

Anya: next steps: I'll author a short RFC with these sections: ownership boundaries, API + headers, HMAC role sig spec, precompute naming + lifecycle, telemetry + SLOs, error contract (403/206), rollout checklist. Will tag security, infra, and devex.

deploy-bot: RFC draft created by Anya at 1795568123: rfc/dashboard-query-interface-split

Oliver: +1. please include an example of a role_bucket policy and an eviction strategy in the RFC.

Mike: also include benchmarks for the suggested p50/p95 numbers and an initial canary plan (10 orgs -> 50 orgs -> opt-in GA).

Anya: done. will post the draft in #eng-architecture and ping reviewers. thanks all :tada:
